title: Prevent Command Not Found creating an empty $PROFILE unless installed

status.label: Likely fix identified
status.detail: Command Not Found checks can create an empty PowerShell $PROFILE even when the module is not installed.

next_action.label: Review the targeted PowerShell script change.

judgment.rationale: The requirement-check script should be observational when the module is not installed; its unconditional profile creation is a direct source-level match for the reported side effect. Keep any intentional profile creation in the actual enable/install path separate.
evidence: Related EnableModule.ps1 contains a distinct profile-creation path; this proposal does not remove that behavior.

proposed_fixes.title: Avoid creating the PowerShell profile during an unmet requirement check
proposed_fixes.root_cause: CheckCmdNotFoundRequirements.ps1 creates the profile as part of checking requirements, even when Command Not Found is not installed.
plan: Inspect the check script’s control flow and distinguish requirement inspection from module enablement.
Guard or remove profile creation from the non-installed check path while preserving intentional creation during enablement.
Add focused tests for an absent profile with the module absent and installed.
verification: Run the check with $PROFILE absent and Command Not Found not installed; verify the profile remains absent.
Verify the module enablement path still creates/configures the profile when required.

confidence.rationale: The current script contains the direct side effect the issue requests removing, and the separate enablement path provides a clear boundary.
